title: Manual dissection of Schistosoma mansoni and S. japonicum for transcriptomic analysis
author: Unknown
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.uq3evyn

steps.title: Prepare Petri dish for microscopy
steps.instruction: Prepare the Petri dish containing worms for observation under the stereomicroscope.

substeps.instruction: Remove the Petri dish from the ice bath.
Touch the dish against a paper to remove excess water.
Place the dish under the stereomicroscope (e.g., Leica EZ4) and adjust the focus.

steps.title: Position the worm head
steps.instruction: Locate and stabilize the head of a parasite for dissection.

substeps.instruction: Identify a parasite with an uncurled head/esophagus.
Increase lens magnification.
Use tweezers (e.g., Ideal Tak 7SG.CX.0) and Vannas scissors (John Weiss 0103123) to keep the head in the field-of-view.

steps.title: Perform first incision
steps.instruction: Make the first incision at the line of the transverse gut.

substeps.instruction: Hold the parasite with tweezers at an angle where suckers are clearly visible (lateral view or suckers facing up).
Make the first incision (#1) along the transverse gut, where the dark pigmentation of hemozoin starts.

steps.title: Collect HE fragment
steps.instruction: Aspirate the detached HE fragment and store it on ice.

substeps.instruction: Use a P20 micropipette to aspirate the floating HE fragment with RNAlater solution.
Dispense the fragment into the HE microtube.
Keep the tube on ice at all times.
Ensure no other fragments or particulate material are aspirated with the HE.

steps.title: Collect BE fragment
steps.instruction: Cut and collect the posterior end of the parasite.

substeps.instruction: Perform a final cut (#2) to remove the posterior third of the parasite body.
Collect the BE fragment using tweezers.
Transfer the fragment to the BE microtube and keep it in the ice box.

steps.title: Clean tools and repeat
steps.instruction: Prepare tools for the next parasite and repeat the dissection process.

substeps.instruction: If salt crystals are present, immerse tweezers and scissors in a beaker of deionized water.
Dry tools with a soft, lint-free paper.
Repeat the dissection steps for additional parasites.

steps.title: Manage temperature and materials
steps.instruction: Maintain sample integrity by chilling the Petri dish every 10 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Start a 10-minute countdown when the Petri dish is removed from the ice.
Return the Petri dish to the ice once the timer expires.
Transfer dissected worms to the 'dissected body' microtube and add new worms to the Petri dish for the next round.
If salt crystals accumulate in the RNAlater solution: discard the solution, wash the Petri dish with deionized water, dry with lint-free paper, and add fresh RNAlater solution.
